signature_blacklisted_ip.description: Traffic matches a known malicious IP signature (IoC). This indicates direct communication with a known threat actor infrastructure.
recommended_actions: Block IP immediately
Quarantine device
Investigate other devices that may have communicated with this IP

signature_suspicious_port.description: Traffic matches a known suspicious port signature (e.g., 4444 for Metasploit).
recommended_actions: Block port at firewall
Investigate device for unauthorized services

brute_force_login.description: Adversaries may use brute force techniques to gain access to accounts when passwords are unknown or when password hashes are obtained. IoT devices are especially vulnerable due to widespread use of default or weak credentials.
recommended_actions: Enforce strong, unique credentials on all IoT devices
Implement account lockout / rate-limiting after repeated failed attempts
Disable default vendor credentials immediately after deployment

port_scan.description: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of services running on remote hosts, including those that may be vulnerable to remote exploitation, as a precursor to further attack.
recommended_actions: Segment IoT devices onto isolated VLANs
Deploy firewall rules restricting unnecessary inbound scanning
Enable intrusion detection on gateway/router

c2_communication.description: Adversaries may communicate using application layer protocols to avoid detection by blending in with existing traffic, often indicating the device has already been compromised and is receiving instructions from a remote server.
recommended_actions: Immediately isolate the affected device from the network
Block identified C2 IP/domain at the firewall
Perform full firmware reset and forensic imaging before restoring device

ddos_traffic.description: Adversaries may perform network denial of service (DoS) attacks to degrade or block availability of targeted resources, often using compromised IoT devices as part of a botnet (e.g., Mirai-style attacks).
recommended_actions: Isolate device from network immediately
Notify upstream ISP/security team if outbound flood is confirmed
Check device for signs of botnet malware and reflash firmware

unauthorized_mqtt_access.description: Adversaries may attempt to subscribe to or publish on MQTT topics without proper authorization, potentially intercepting or manipulating sensor data flowing through the broker.
recommended_actions: Enforce authentication and TLS on the MQTT broker
Apply topic-level access control lists (ACLs)
Audit broker logs for unauthorized subscribe/publish attempts

known_cve_exploit.description: Adversaries may exploit a known vulnerability in device firmware or an exposed service to gain initial access to the device.
recommended_actions: Update device firmware to the latest patched version
Restrict remote/public access to the device's management interface
Add device to a watchlist for continued monitoring

botnet_signature_match.description: Traffic pattern matches known signatures associated with Mirai-family IoT botnet malware, indicating likely infection and recruitment into a botnet for future coordinated attacks.
recommended_actions: Immediately isolate and reboot device (Mirai is often memory-resident)
Change all credentials before reconnecting device
Apply firmware update and enable auto-update if available
